card.name: Words just before a risk statement
card.fires_on: Words right before a risk or likelihood phrase, such as a comma after a risk factor, or 'reduce' or 'the' before 'risk of'. It appears in risk-factor and family-history sentences and in drug-label risk warnings.

modes.label: Risk factor then outcome
modes.description: A comma or noun ending a risk-factor clause, just before 'more likely' or 'at risk' wording.
modes.example: If you have a strong family history of cancer<<,>> you may be more likely to develop cancer

modes.label: Before 'risk of' in labels
modes.description: A verb or article right before the phrase 'risk of' in a drug-label warning.
modes.example: Consider a lower dose of insulin or insulin secretagogue to<< reduce>> risk of hypoglycemia when

card.writes: It suppresses 'likely' and 'unlikely' words and promotes words starting with P, so it steers away from likelihood wording at that spot.
card.plain: It fires on the word just before a sentence says someone is more likely to get a condition or faces a risk.
